chapter_theme: Thirumula Nayanar Njanam, nine verses attributed to Tirumular but not found in the Tirumanthiram, is a single meditation on the letter A as the foot (பாதம்) and the root (மூலம்): the A is the Lord who stands as he and she, the root is the mooladhara circle with its triangle and three nadis, and the practice is to look daily at this foot through the sushumna to the brow, seeing the guru as Isa. The light is beyond male, female and neuter, and the Vedas that search for it find only void.
structure_note: 1613 to 1615 define the A as foot, root and all; 1616 and 1617 give the practice of looking; 1618 identifies teacher and Lord; 1619 to 1621 locate the foot in the sushumna where the two lights rise and set and gather all into the one letter. Each verse opens with the last word of the one before (அணுவதாமே / அதுவாகி, நோக்கே / நோக்கமுடன், ஆசானாமே / ஆசானும்), as an antadi.

1613.reading: Becoming the foot and becoming what is beyond the cosmos, the letter called A itself becoming the foot; becoming crown and middle, in the root becoming the three things and the first; becoming the step and, free of the three voids, the supreme light Lord beyond the steps; the root that is the foot becoming A and standing as he and she: that state is the atom.
1613.nuance: அகாரம் (the letter A) is made the Lord's foot, the first of the letters as he is the first of things. முப்பொருள் may be pati, pasu and pasam or the three lights; முப்பாழ், the three voids, is a Tirumanthiram term for the voids of maya, knowledge and their traces. The last word அணு (atom) is unexplained: the Siddhar formula is that the Lord is at once atom and whole.

1614.reading: Becoming That, becoming he and she, becoming all; beginning, middle and end, the undivided whole; common to all, the refuge of every life, the root of every thing; honey, the bee and the taste, the flower and the scent, beyond reckoning: the A that is That becoming the root is the root that holds up all the cosmos.
1614.nuance: The chain of ஆகி (becoming) is the Siddhar way of stating pervasion: honey, bee, taste, flower and scent are one sweetness seen five ways. புகலிடம், refuge, is the one relational word in a verse of identities.

1615.reading: The root is the circle of the adhara: the three lights, the triangle, the three nadis; the water of the Sivalinga's feet called good conduct; it is the holy feet, the holy body and the dance; holding up all the cosmos with its form, the pillar that has sprouted and looks upward; the whole throat that drank the poison standing as itself: know the letter that begins with A, and see.
1615.nuance: The mooladhara is given its usual marks, the triangle and the three channels (ida, pingala, sushumna); முச்சுடர் (three lights) are sun, moon and fire. கம்பம் (pillar) is the spine or the lingam read as the axis of the body. ஆலமுண்ட கண்டம் is Siva's poison-stained throat, so the body's centres are read as the Lord's own body.

1616.reading: What is known is the supreme beyond, which is A; the knowing U is the supreme consciousness; what is born, the whole world, is the sects, and all the kinds of instruments called difference; knowing the foot called A as foot and crown, look at it every day.
1616.nuance: Only six lines survive of an eight-line stanza. A is தற்பரம் and U is சிற்பரம், a Vedanta-coloured pairing of the Om's letters rather than the Tirumanthiram's Siva and Shakti; the born world is lumped with சமயம் (sects) and கருவி (the tattvas) as the realm of difference. அரிந்ததுவும் is probably a slip for அறிந்ததுவும்.

1617.reading: With intent look at the foot called the root within the supreme consciousness, the subtle thing; firmly, crossing past the kinds of adharas, look at the place between the holy eyes, the nose and the brow; those who know the way and can look at this state here are sons of the one with twisted locks; those who daily stand looking at the guru as a flame of grace become teachers.
1617.nuance: The practice is stated plainly for once: gaze fixed at the brow centre (புருவமத்தி) after passing the lower adharas. The verse ends with the guru, and the next takes the word up: looking at the guru is itself the way to become one.

1618.reading: Teacher and Isa are one; he and she are one; it is That itself; the unspoken mantra is this too; it is the form of the great light, and the name; all the arts that are loved are itself; it is the firm seat of Omkara; for those who here see Isa as the teacher, Kailasa may be reached with joy.
1618.nuance: பேசாத மந்திரம், the unspoken mantra, is the ajapa, the breath itself as recitation, as tradition takes it. பூடம் is a form of பீடம் (seat). The verse grants Kailasa 'here' (இங்கு), in the body, to one who sees the Lord as the guru, an inversion of the usual 'see the guru as the Lord'.

1619.reading: In the root of the hard-to-reach Paramasiva, the place where the two lights rise and set; the sushumna, where the body's working ceases, becoming the pillar, stands settled as the light that is the true thing; in this way, worship the foot called the root at the place where the two times are no more, and see.
1619.nuance: இருசுடர், the two lights, are sun and moon, which in the cipher are the right and left breaths; the sushumna is where they rise and sink. இருநேரம் அற்றிடம், the place without the two times, may mean beyond day and night or beyond the two breaths. The first two lines are printed twice with small variants, which looks like a doubled couplet.

1620.reading: What is seen is the vision of the great light, ... when it shows itself as the thing; becoming male, female and neuter, and becoming the foot, the light seated beyond the beyond; all the Vedas practised in vain searched and did not see it and stood settled as mere void; the world-light practised afar, its root: look clearly at it as the foot hard to seek.
1620.nuance: Line 2 is a fragment (பொருளாகுங் காட்டும் போதே), so the sense of the opening is incomplete. வீண்பயிலும் வேதம் calls Vedic study vain, and வெறும்பாழ் (mere void) is what the Vedas end in, a negative use of a word the Siddhars elsewhere use for the goal. ஆண் பெண்ணாய் அலியாகி, male, female and neuter, is the Tirumanthiram's formula for the Lord beyond gender.

1621.reading: The foot hard to make clear becoming the A-letter, becoming itself the supreme consciousness and the supreme beyond, becoming the light hard to destroy, settled as beginning, middle and end; becoming the first hard to speak, becoming the root, becoming the three lights, the completed light; in the whirl becoming the point, becoming ..., the one letter hard to ...: gather it all into that and see.
1621.nuance: சுழியினிலே முனையாகி splits சுழுமுனை into its parts, whirl and point, as a gloss on the name. கோப மாகி is unclear (anger does not fit; perhaps a corrupt கோபுரம், tower). The last line has lost its first syllable (லரிய for சொல்லரிய, hard to speak) and முடிந்த் is a broken form. The sense is clear enough: all the names of the chapter resolve into the one letter.

links.note: Both open with the letter A as first: the Kural makes the Primal Lord first of the world as A is first of the letters; this text goes further and makes the A itself the Lord's foot and the root of the body.

Sivavakkiyar sets the fire in the triangle with the letter A placed in it; here the root circle has the triangle, three lights and three nadis, and the letter beginning with A is what one must know there.

Both read the letters of Om as a pair, but differently: Tirumular makes A the Lord and U the Lady spread through the world; this text makes A the supreme beyond (தற்பரம்) and U the supreme consciousness (சிற்பரம்), a Vedantic rather than a Siva-Shakti pairing.
Tirumular says the guru is Siva and people do not grasp it; this text says teacher and Isa are one and that those who see Isa as the teacher reach Kailasa here.

Tirumular has moon and sun rising and falling through ida and pingala with life welling up in the middle; here the two lights rise and set in the root of Paramasiva and the sushumna between them is the pillar of light.
Both describe the light as neither woman, man nor neuter and as beyond knowing: Tirumular says no one can know it, this text says the Vedas searched and found only void.

Here the Vedas practised in vain search and stand as mere void; the Valluvar text allows that the Veda's hidden knowledge, if it becomes true perception, leads by grace to the state. The two texts in the same collection disagree on whether the Veda can be a path.

source_issues: 1616 has six lines where the other stanzas have eight; two lines are missing.
1619 lines 1-2 are repeated as lines 3-4 with minor spelling variants (பரமசிவத்தின் / பரசிவத்தின்), probably a doubled couplet.
1620 line 2 is a fragment (பொருளாகுங் காட்டும் போதே).
1621 line 8 has lost its first syllable (லரிய) and line 6 has a broken form (முடிந்த்).
